commands.name: amend
commands.desc: Modify an approved plan through conversation.
commands.body:
# /sinter:amend

Load `plan.json`. Apply the change through `writing-plans` conventions.
Regenerate `PLAN.md`. Preserve completed-task state.

Re-run `judges` on `grounding` and `completeness` if the change is structural.

Report what moved, what was added, what was dropped.

commands.name: audit
commands.desc: Simplification, dead code, and technical debt.
commands.body:
# /sinter:audit

Route to `simplification` for working code.

- `--simplify` (default) - apply the ladder to existing code
- `--dead` - unreferenced exports, unreachable branches, unused dependencies
- `--debt` - inventory with cost framing for `technical-influence`

Behavior-preserving. Anything that changes behavior is a separate change with
its own tests. Invariant 4 binds - validation, error handling, security, and
accessibility are not removable.

commands.name: build
commands.desc: Main entry. Implement, fix, or change code. Routes by depth lane.
commands.body:
# /sinter:build

Route to `router` first. It selects the lane and states it in one line.

Then, per lane:

- **lazy** - `understanding-first`, then `principles` ladder. One runnable
  check if the logic is non-trivial.
- **standard** - `understanding-first`, `test-driven-development` (red/green),
  `principles` correctness bar. State tradeoffs.
- **full** - hand off to `/sinter:plan`. Do not implement before the gate.

Load stack packs via `stack-detect`. If no pack matches, `language-agnostic`
and say which tier.

`--lane` overrides inference. Escalation rules in `router` still apply and
still announce themselves.

commands.name: comply
commands.desc: Assess technical controls against a framework and export evidence.
commands.body:
# /sinter:comply

Route to `compliance`.

Frameworks: soc2, iso27001, iso42001, gdpr, hipaa, dora, fedramp, cmmc, pci.

1. Retrieve current control text (`docs-lookup`) - never assess from memory
2. Run `scripts/assess.mjs` deterministic checks
3. Map results through `controls/crosswalk.json`
4. Report per control: met, gap, needs-human-evidence, or not-assessable

`--evidence` exports the artifact bundle.

**Every report states the boundary: Sinter assesses, it does not certify.** A
control is never `met` on inference.

commands.name: debug
commands.desc: Systematic debugging. Root cause before any fix.
commands.body:
# /sinter:debug

Route to `systematic-debugging`. All four phases, in order.

Do not propose a fix before phase 1 produces a one-sentence mechanism
statement. If the root cause lands in a shared function, `router` escalates -
say so.

commands.name: design
commands.desc: Frontend design work - critique, polish, layout, motion, hardening.
commands.body:
# /sinter:design

Route to `design`. Lens is one of: critique, polish, distill, bolder, quieter,
layout, typeset, colorize, animate, harden, delight.

Reads `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` if present; asks audience and brand-vs-product
if not.

Runs `scripts/detectors.mjs` first - deterministic, no model.

Accessibility findings route to `accessibility` and are not styling
preferences.

commands.name: fix
commands.desc: Act on findings from a prior review.
commands.body:
# /sinter:fix

Load findings from the last `review-engine` run.

Verify each finding still applies before acting on it - the code may have
changed. Fix in severity order. Each fix follows the lane's test policy.

Re-run `verification-before-completion` before reporting. Report what was
fixed, what was deliberately not, and why.

commands.name: help
commands.desc: What Sinter can do, and when each part fires.
commands.body:
# /sinter:help

No arguments: the command surface, the current lane and dials, and the loaded
stack packs.

With an argument: what that skill does, when it fires, and what it explicitly
does not cover.

With ~48 skills, this is not a nicety - a capability nobody can find is a
capability that does not exist.

commands.name: improve
commands.desc: Review improvement proposals Sinter has drafted from recurring patterns.
commands.body:
# /sinter:improve

Route to `self-improvement`.

- `list` (default) - open proposals, newest first, with the pattern, the
  recurrence count, and a one-line summary of the change.
- `show <n>` - the full proposal: the pattern, the diff, and the learnings that
  evidence it.
- `accept <n>` - apply the reviewed diff through the normal flow, committing at
  the configured autonomy level.
- `reject <n>` - drop it; not re-proposed unless substantially new evidence
  appears.
- `defer <n>` - keep it open, do not surface it again this session.

Sinter only proposes. Accepting is the human review step, and it is the only
way a proposal becomes a change. See `self-improvement` for why the boundary
is where it is.

commands.name: init
commands.body:
# /sinter:init

1. `stack-detect` - identify ecosystems per workspace
2. `codebase-onboarding` - architecture map, conventions, entry points
3. Write `sinter.config.json` with detected defaults
4. Write or update `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` with project conventions
5. `--design` also writes `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` (`design`)
6. `--scaffold-pack` writes a tier-3 pack to `.sinter/packs/` for an ecosystem
   with no curated pack

Idempotent. Re-running updates rather than duplicating.

commands.name: learn
commands.body:
# /sinter:learn

Route to `memory`.

`capture` applies the four-part quality bar before writing - durable,
non-obvious, actionable, specific. Rejections say which test failed.

`prune` removes stale, contradicted, never-triggered, and duplicate entries.
Run it periodically; an unpruned store silently degrades every session.

commands.name: loop
commands.desc: Run unattended iteration over specs or a plan.
commands.body:
# /sinter:loop

Route to `autonomy`.

Default level `commit` - commits locally, never pushes. `--level` overrides
for this run only; persist it in `sinter.config.json` if it should stick.

`autonomous` requires an explicit branch target and will refuse without one.

Runs in a worktree at `commit` and `autonomous`. Halts on the conditions in
`autonomy`. Rails in `hooks/pre-tool-use.sh` bind at every level.

commands.name: mode
commands.desc: Set lane, dials, and autonomy level.
commands.body:
# /sinter:mode

No arguments: report the current settings and where each came from
(inline, session, project config, user config, or default).

Session-scoped unless written to `sinter.config.json`.

Resolution order:
`inline flag > session /mode > ./sinter.config.json > ~/.sinter/config.json > defaults`

commands.name: plan
commands.desc: Write an implementation plan. Full lane. Stops at the human gate.
commands.body:
# /sinter:plan

1. `understanding-first`, and `codebase-onboarding` if the repo is unfamiliar
2. `writing-specs` if acceptance criteria do not exist yet
3. `writing-plans` - produces `plan.json` and `PLAN.md`
4. `judges` on `spec-quality` and `grounding`
5. **Stop.** Present the plan. Wait for approval.

Do not implement. The gate is the point of this command.

commands.name: review
commands.desc: Multi-agent code review of a diff or PR.
commands.body:
# /sinter:review

Route to `review-engine`.

Default scope: uncommitted changes, then the current branch against its base.
`--since` overrides. `--pr` fetches the PR diff and posts inline comments.

`--depth shallow` runs hygiene and the correctness reviewer only. `deep` adds
cross-file, security, tests, and conventions reviewers.

If any changed file touches a controlled surface, `compliance` runs in
continuous mode and its findings are included.

commands.name: stats
commands.desc: Token and cost attribution for this session.
commands.body:
# /sinter:stats

Reads the session transcript. Reports tokens and estimated cost by skill,
agent, or phase.

Useful for tuning `judges.routing` and finding a reviewer fleet that costs
more than it returns.

controls.title: Unique identification of users
controls.check: No shared or generic accounts in the identity provider or application user table

controls.title: Least privilege authorization
controls.check: Every endpoint authorizes at the resource; no client-supplied role or tenant is trusted

controls.title: Encryption in transit
controls.check: TLS 1.2 minimum on all external listeners; certificate verification enabled

controls.title: Encryption at rest
controls.check: Data stores encrypted; keys managed outside the data store

controls.title: Audit logging of security events
controls.check: Authentication, authorization failure, and privileged action are logged with actor, action, and timestamp

controls.title: Log integrity and retention
controls.check: Audit logs are append-only or tamper-evident and retained per policy

controls.title: Change management
controls.check: Changes are peer-reviewed and traceable to an approved request

controls.title: Dependency vulnerability management
controls.check: Dependency audit runs in CI; lockfile committed; known-critical advisories fail the build

controls.title: Backup and restore
controls.check: Backups exist, are encrypted, and a restore has been executed and recorded
controls.note: Backup configuration is checkable; a rehearsed restore requires human evidence

controls.title: Data subject rights
controls.check: Access, export, and deletion paths exist and are exercised end to end

controls.title: Data minimization and retention
controls.check: Retention configured per data class; no unbounded PII retention

controls.title: AI system impact assessment
controls.check: Deployed model or agent has a recorded impact assessment and documented data provenance
controls.note: Provenance records are checkable; the assessment itself requires human sign-off

controls.title: Operational resilience testing
controls.check: Failure modes exercised; recovery objectives measured against a test
